subject: Emergency throughput addendum & temporary overrun terms
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing an unexpected traffic surge tied to a partner promo this week — token usage has spiked to ~4x our forecasted daily baseline and is pushing us against your imposed quota. We need a short-term throughput uplift for ~2 weeks while we finalize the Dedicated capacity contract.

Two asks: 1) Can Redwood enable a temporary throughput top-up for the next 14 calendar days so our app doesn't degrade? 2) How will overrun charges be invoiced/credited — can we get a cap or a provisional grace period while procurement completes the PO?

I've attached a brief usage snapshot (finlytics_usage_snapshot_nov.csv) and included procurement on this thread. We can share more telemetry if needed.

Thanks — urgent but not catastrophic; want to avoid throttles and paging.

Anna Lopez
Head of Product
Finlytics
anna.lopez@finlytics.com
+1 415 555 0199

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

Thanks for the heads up, Anna — and thanks for attaching the snapshot. Sorry you're seeing that surge. We're able to support a temporary uplift while you finalize Dedicated, but need to lock a few guardrails so it's clear how overrun charges will be handled.

High-level proposal (quick):
- Temporary throughput top-up: +3x baseline concurrent throughput for 14 calendar days, starting upon approval.
- Billing: overrun billed at standard overage rate, with an optional one-time credit if you convert this month to a Dedicated commit (details in draft).
- Grace: 48-hour billing grace window from uplift start (i.e., no invoices issued until we confirm procurement path).

Marcus — can you confirm the technical opt-in and estimate per-token/peaked-hour cost?
Priyom — can you draft the short addendum language we can sign quickly (14-day term, threshold, cap, credit on conversion)?

Anna — if the above sounds reasonable I'll push a draft addendum + cost estimate back by EOD. If procurement already has a PO number, send it and we'll tag the invoice.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
(650) 555-0132

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus — can you confirm the technical opt-in and estimate per-token/peaked-hour cost?

Hi all — quick tech/cost note. We can enable a short-lived throughput uplift through a burst policy (no infra change) with the following guardrails:
- Mode: temporary burst (runtime policy) with a hard ceiling to prevent runaway costs.
- Recommendation: +3x baseline concurrency, cap at 12k RPS (matches observed peak in the snapshot).
- KV cache warm-up: expect ~10–20% latency increase for first 6 hours; recommend pre-warming keys if you can.

Cost (rough estimate):
- Overage rate (standard): $0.0009 / token for high-priority bursts.
- If we enable a capped overrun (suggest cap = $12k total for the 14 days) you'll avoid surprise bills above that amount.
- If Finlytics converts to a Dedicated commit within 30 days, propose a credit equal to 50% of overage charges applied to the first month of Dedicated billing (not to exceed $12k).

I've attached a spreadsheet (throughput-cost-estimate.xlsx) with a couple scenarios. If you want a lower per-token rate we can discuss a short-term discounted surcharge (e.g., 10–15%) in exchange for a formal short addendum.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

Anna — thanks for flagging procurement.

I put together a short-form addendum draft (attached as draft-addendum-Redwood-Finlytics.pdf). Key legal/econ points:
- Term: 14 calendar days, effective upon activation.
- Thresholds: burst uplift will be limited to +3x baseline or 12k RPS, whichever is lower.
- Billing: overrun billed at the agreed overage rate with a hard cap of $15,000 for the term.
- Conversion credit: if Finlytics signs a Dedicated commit within 30 days, Redwood will credit 50% of overrun charges up to $15,000 against the first invoice.
- Invoicing: Redwood will issue an interim invoice; if procurement provides PO before invoice issuance, we will place the invoice on hold and withhold charging for up to 72 hours to allow PO processing.
- SLA: this temporary uplift does not alter the base SLA; however, Redwood will prioritize traffic routing for performance during the uplift window.

If that looks OK we can route the addendum for signatures via DocuSign. If you'd like a lower cap than $15k, we can discuss increasing the conversion credit instead.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

Thanks Priyom — the draft looks close. A couple small asks from our side: 1) could you reduce the hard cap to $10k and increase the conversion-credit to 60% (applied to the first 2 months) if we convert within 21 days? 2) We need a 3-business-day window to get the PO processed before charges post — 72 hours is tight for our AP.

Also, does this uplift change any rate-limiting behavior for our bot users? We want to ensure user experience is consistent.

Procurement will attach a PO but it may take a day or two to land. PO reference: FIN-PO-2026-1109 (we'll send the PDF shortly).

—Anna

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Emergency throughput bump + billing for Nov spike

Great — thanks for the quick turn, Anna. Final position after internal alignment:
- Term: 14 calendar days starting when Finlytics confirms activation.
- Limits: +3x baseline up to 12k RPS.
- Billing cap: $12,000 hard cap (compromise between our $15k and your $10k).
- Conversion credit: 60% of overrun charges applied to first 2 invoices if Finlytics signs Dedicated within 21 days (cap $12k).
- PO window: we will hold charges for up to 5 business days after invoice issuance to accommodate AP (extended from 72 hours).
- Rate-limiting: no change to base rate-limiting rules; the uplift is a routing/policy change to allow higher concurrency — Marcus: confirm there will be no per-user throttling changes other than higher concurrency headroom.

Next steps: 1) Priyom will upload the final addendum to DocuSign (related link). 2) Anna/procurement sends PO PDF (FIN-PO-2026-1109) and indicate desired activation date. 3) Upon DocuSign signature we will enable the uplift and monitor.

I've attached the final addendum and the cost estimate to this thread. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/finish/XYZ-ADDENDUM-2026

If everyone is good, Priyom — please start the signature routing. Anna — happy to flip the switch as soon as you confirm an activation date.

Thanks,
